title: Normalize and persist provider run telemetry
description: Objective: compose raw production provider telemetry with the landed scheduler usage authority at the daemon boundary that can depend on both packages. Deliverable: a focused daemon telemetry adapter/codec/ledger that consumes @moe/runner launch telemetry, runs every usage envelope through @moe/scheduler normalizeUsageMeasurement, preserves upstream versus scheduler refusal provenance, and commits one immutable digest-bound provider-run record for downstream benchmark reads. Hard dependencies: task-5fa25bb33e974f04865b46f9fa0f3910 and task-cbc42f3383444c05a20c6bf56129e8c8; production dispatch consumer is task-6cbff01023b14b26a78fc5e3eb1dd8a9. NOT in scope: launching providers, benchmark statistics, pricing comparison, confirmatory corpus, or claims. Owned paths: focused apps/daemon/src/telemetry/** production/test modules; use existing SqliteEventStore event/decision APIs and no new schema. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/runner test && pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test.
definitionOfDone: Daemon composition imports only @moe/runner and @moe/scheduler public roots, validates one raw launch-bound telemetry handoff, and delegates every usage envelope in original provider sequence to production normalizeUsageMeasurement without copying its source/coverage matrix.

One frozen canonical provider-run record binds run/effect/attempt, selected and provider-observed model evidence, effort, runtime/profile identities, wall/monotonic timestamps, exact terminal/infra/count/concurrency facts, normalized usage rows, cost-basis metadata, raw receipt digests, and a record digest.

UNKNOWN usage retains quantity null and exact upstream code/layer; PARTIAL retains its measured lower bound; scheduler CONTRACT/MEASUREMENT failures preserve their exact code/layer separately and no client-estimated Claude cost becomes ACTUAL_BILLED.

Existing SqliteEventStore decision/event APIs durably commit exactly one content-bound record; replay is idempotent, changed-byte replay/conflict fails closed, malformed/truncated/digest-mismatched reads return a stable telemetry unreadable code/layer, and no bespoke SQLite schema is added.

Focused real-store tests cover COMPLETE/PARTIAL/UNKNOWN, every declared source with exact non-zero cardinality, lost-ack/reopen and conflict behavior, and mutation-check production coverage plus model/effort bindings.
Fresh pnpm --filter @moe/runner test && pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test exits 0.
taskRails: Daemon is the direction-safe composition boundary; runner must not depend on scheduler and tests must not inject a fake normalizer.
Preserve upstream provider reason code/layer separately from scheduler CONTRACT/MEASUREMENT code/layer; do not flatten or invent a pass.
No new store schema/table; use public event/decision transactions and strict canonical bytes.
This task lands the durable composition surface; task-6cbff01023b14b26a78fc5e3eb1dd8a9 remains the real live dispatch consumer and must be named in the handoff.

implementationPlan.description:
RE-MEASURE AT THE THEN-CURRENT HEAD AND READ THE TEMPLATE. No production bytes written.

1. `git rev-parse --short HEAD` and `ls apps/daemon/src/telemetry/ 2>&1` — the directory must still be ABSENT. If it now exists, a sibling slice has started; STOP and report blocked rather than colliding in the shared worktree.
2. RE-RUN THE DEPENDENCY-EDGE PROBE WITH BOTH CONTROLS, probe deleted in the same command via a shell trap so no probe file can survive into a commit (epic rail 5). Positive: import `normalizeUsageMeasurement` and type `UsageMeasurementRecord` from "@moe/scheduler" and `parseClaudeResultTelemetry` from "@moe/runner" through the BARE specifier; `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` must exit 0. Negative: import a symbol that cannot exist; it must fail TS2305 with exit 1. WITHOUT THE NEGATIVE CONTROL A PASS IS NOT EVIDENCE — a probe that was never compiled also 'passes'.
3. Note for the record: `grep telemetry packages/runner/src/index.ts` returns ZERO hits and is a FALSE NEGATIVE. The surface is re-exported through `export * from "./surface/claude-surface.js"` at index.ts:162. Do not report blocked on that grep.
4. READ THE TEMPLATE END TO END before designing anything: apps/daemon/src/activation/activation-ledger-contracts.ts. This plan mirrors its decomposition deliberately — deviating is a decision to justify, not a default.
5. Read the producer shapes this contract binds: `ClaudeTelemetryHandoff` (claude-telemetry-launch.ts:70-86), `ProviderRunRef` and the refusal types (provider-telemetry-contracts.ts:118-147), and `UsageMeasurementRecord` + `ObservedIntervalRefs` (budget-contract.ts).

TESTS FIRST (TDD), and write them so they cannot pass vacuously.

Create `apps/daemon/src/telemetry/provider-run-contracts.test.ts`. Most of this module is types, which vanish at runtime and cannot be asserted — so the tests that carry weight are the ones over the RUNTIME values. Do NOT write a test that imports the module and checks it is defined; that passes for any file.

Assert:
- The closed reason-code array's EXACT membership, and its length derived from the imported array itself rather than a hand-typed number, so adding a code without updating the test is impossible and removing one reddens.
- The layer array's exact membership, same discipline.
- Both arrays are FROZEN. A forgotten `Object.freeze` is invisible until something mutates a shared array at runtime; assert `Object.isFrozen` directly.
- The aggregate-id derivation is deterministic and INJECTIVE over the identity fields it binds: two run refs differing in exactly one field must produce different aggregate ids, asserted field by field. A derivation that silently ignores one field is the defect this test exists to catch, and it is invisible to a round-trip test.
- The unreadable-record code is present in the vocabulary (slices 2 and 4 both import it).

These tests will not compile until the next step lands; that is the intended TDD order.

THE FROZEN CANONICAL RECORD (DoD 2). Create `apps/daemon/src/telemetry/provider-run-contracts.ts` and declare the `ProviderRunRecord` interface, every field readonly.

Bind the producer shapes VERBATIM rather than re-deriving them — re-declaring a field the producer already models is the silent-duplicate defect:
- Run/effect/attempt identity: bind `ProviderRunRef` whole (it is exactly `{provider, runRef, effectIntentId, attemptRef, epoch}`), not three hand-rolled id fields.
- Selected AND provider-observed model evidence as TWO SEPARATE fields (`declared` and `observedModel`). A selection is not an observation, and collapsing them destroys the only evidence that the provider ran what was asked for.
- Effort, runtime and profile identities.
- Wall and monotonic timestamps, kept distinct — they answer different questions and a single timestamp field cannot serve both.
- Exact terminal, infrastructure, count-coverage and concurrency facts, typed against the runner's published `ProviderTerminalOutcome`, `ProviderInfrastructureOutcome`, `ProviderCountCoverage`, `ProviderConcurrencyFact`.
- Normalized usage rows typed as the scheduler's `UsageMeasurementRecord` (import `ObservedIntervalRefs` too — without it a consumer can name the record but never construct one).
- Cost-basis metadata, the raw receipt digests, and the record digest.
- TWO SEPARATE provenance fields: the upstream `ProviderTelemetryRefusal {code, layer}` and the scheduler's `LayeredIssue {layer, code}`. Task rail 2 forbids flattening them, and the shape is fixed HERE — if this contract gives them one field, slice 3 cannot comply.

Import every producer type from the `@moe/runner` / `@moe/scheduler` package ROOTS by bare specifier. A deep path fails TS6059 and this repo has no escape hatch.

THE CLOSED VOCABULARIES, THE NARROW STORE PORT, AND THE AGGREGATE DERIVATION — same file as step 3, kept a separate step because these are the parts later slices inherit and cannot renegotiate.

- CLOSED, frozen reason-code array in the `Object.freeze([...] as const)` style of activation-ledger-contracts.ts:65, with a derived union type. Include the stable UNREADABLE-RECORD code now, even though slice 1 has no reader for it: slices 2 and 4 both import it, and omitting it forces slice 2 to invent a local one — precisely the duplicate-authority defect this family exists to avoid. Add a frozen layer array so every refusal can name its layer.
- THE NARROW STORE PORT. Name ONLY `commitExpectedVersionDecision`, `getCommandDecision` and the aggregate read slice 4 needs for its replay answer. DO NOT name `commitWithApply` or `commitExpectedVersionDecisionWithApply`. Those hand the callback a raw `DatabaseSync` and exist for callers that write their own tables, which the no-new-schema rail forbids; activation-ledger-contracts.ts:172-178 uses exactly this technique to make the mistake unreachable rather than merely discouraged. THIS IS THE ONLY SLICE THAT CAN BUILD THIS GUARD — a wide port here hands slice 4 a loaded gun that no test will catch.
- THE DERIVED AGGREGATE ID, bound to the run identity so one provider run is one aggregate head. This is what lets slice 4 borrow conflict detection from the store's expected-version check instead of hand-rolling one.

Run the step-2 tests; they must now pass. Confirm the file is under 250 lines with `grep -c ''` (the template equivalent is 244, so this is a real constraint — if it overruns, split the vocabularies into their own module rather than trimming the record).

THE `.js` BRIDGE AND THE STRUCTURAL CHECKS. Create `apps/daemon/src/telemetry/provider-run-contracts.js` with bytes EXACTLY `export * from "./provider-run-contracts.ts";` followed by a single LF newline.

This is not boilerplate: a new production module without its sibling bridge is caught by NEITHER tsc NOR vitest, so the omission ships silently and breaks a consumer slice later. Verify the bytes rather than eyeballing them — compare against the same-shaped bridge at apps/daemon/src/activation/activation-ledger-contracts.js, and confirm LF (not CRLF) line endings, since this repo ships on Windows and an editor may helpfully convert them.

The test file gets NO bridge — that is the measured convention (activation-ledger-fixtures.ts has none).

Also confirm here:
- `apps/daemon/src/index.ts` is UNCHANGED. index-surface.test.ts:267 pins `EXPECTED_EXPORTS.length` to 61; publishing anything new from the daemon root reddens a test outside this slice's scope. The activation ledger family is deliberately unpublished and this family follows it.
- No probe, scratch, or generated evidence file remains anywhere under apps/daemon/src/telemetry/ — epic rail 5.

MUTATION DRILLS (epic rail 6). Every assertion added in step 2 must be proven load-bearing; a green suite is not evidence. For each drill: capture `sha256sum` of the target BEFORE mutating, mutate the PRODUCTION surface, run the focused suite, record which NAMED test reddened and ON WHICH ASSERTION, restore by Edit, then verify the restore by `sha256sum` against the captured hash.

Required drills, each naming the test that must go red:
- D1 VOCABULARY MEMBERSHIP. Remove one member from the reason-code array. The membership test must redden. If the test derives its expected list from the same array it is asserting, it is comparing the array with itself and will stay green — that is the failure this drill exists to expose, and the fix is to pin the names literally while deriving only the COUNT.
- D2 FREEZE. Drop the `Object.freeze` from a vocabulary array. The `Object.isFrozen` assertion must redden.
- D3 AGGREGATE INJECTIVITY. Make the aggregate derivation ignore one identity field (for example, drop `attemptRef` from the input it hashes). The field-by-field injectivity test must redden on THAT field. A derivation silently ignoring a field would let two different runs collide on one aggregate head — which would surface, much later, as slice 4 rejecting a legitimate second run as a conflict.

RESTORE BY sha256, NEVER by `git diff` (blind to untracked paths — every file in this slice is new and untracked, so an empty diff proves nothing) and NEVER by `git checkout` (reverts to HEAD, destroying all of this task's uncommitted work).

A focused vitest run needs `--root .` or it matches ZERO tests and a drill that reddened nothing reads exactly like a drill that found nothing.

GATE, ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, COMMIT.

GATE (DoD 6) — each leg's exit code read SEPARATELY; a `&&`-chained run stops at the first red and reports one status for several legs, and a piped run reports the pipe's tail:
1. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck; echo "TYPECHECK_EXIT=$?"`
2. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test; echo "TEST_EXIT=$?"`
Also run the runner and scheduler legs named in the task's verification line and record them separately — this slice does not import them at runtime, so a red there is almost certainly foreign; attribute it by path under the path-attributed-baseline rail (merge-base failures, HEAD failures, delta intersected with `apps/daemon/src/telemetry/**`, which must be EMPTY) and disclose it verbatim rather than repairing it.

`grep -c ''` the production file: under 250 lines.

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW — invoke the adversarial-self-review skill, then check the items specific to this slice:
1. Does the store port name `commitWithApply` or `commitExpectedVersionDecisionWithApply`? If yes, remove them — that guard is this slice's job and no later test can recover it.
2. Are the two provenance vocabularies in SEPARATE record fields? If they share one, slice 3 cannot comply with task rail 2 and will have to reopen this task.
3. Did any producer type get re-declared locally instead of imported from the package root? Re-declaring a modelled field is a silent duplicate.
4. Is the unreadable-record code present, so slice 2 does not have to invent one?
5. Does any comment claim a guarantee the code does not discharge?

COMMIT BY EXPLICIT PATHSPEC naming only the three `apps/daemon/src/telemetry/provider-run-contracts.*` paths. Never `git add -A` (epic rail 3). If a foreign whole-tree commit has already swept your bytes in, do NOT amend, reset, or re-commit to claim it — hand QA the base-ref diff over the owned paths.

HANDOFF MUST NAME THE CONSUMERS (Clause 1): this slice lands a contract with no runtime consumer yet, which is permitted ONLY by naming the tasks that will compose it — task-fc6581042426444a826981943f441908 (canonical codec) and task-1a7ff170ee544a3a8a10962c25e2ca5b (durable ledger), with task-ea27beb6e1954d0e9dba8ad49cc1641e (normalize composition) as the third sibling. State plainly that DoD items 1, 3, 4 and the real-store half of 5 now belong to those siblings and that this task's DoD needs re-scoping to slice 1.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
SUBMITTED A 10-STEP / 17-FILE SINGLE PLAN FIRST; THE DAEMON HARD-REJECTED IT (max 10 distinct files) and instructed a SPIDR split. That rejection was correct and I am recording it rather than hiding it: the original task bundled four genuinely separable deliverables, and the `.js` bridge convention silently doubles the production file count.

SPLIT ALONG SPIDR Data -> Interface -> Rules -> Path, four slices of three files each:
- SLICE 1 = THIS TASK: the provider-run record contract, its closed reason-code/layer vocabularies, the narrow store port and the aggregate-id derivation. Executable immediately, no new dependency.
- SLICE 2 = task-fc6581042426444a826981943f441908, canonical codec (bytes, digest, unreadable-read path).
- SLICE 3 = task-ea27beb6e1954d0e9dba8ad49cc1641e, the normalize composition against production normalizeUsageMeasurement.
- SLICE 4 = task-1a7ff170ee544a3a8a10962c25e2ca5b, the durable ledger; it closes the family and carries the four-leg gate plus the consumer-edge declaration for task-6cbff01023b14b26a78fc5e3eb1dd8a9.
Each sibling carries the full measurement below in its own description so no architect re-derives it, and each names its hard dependencies.

*** DoD RE-SCOPE REQUIRED - READ THIS BEFORE REVIEWING ***
This task's stored DoD still describes the WHOLE pre-split scope. After the daemon-mandated split, only DoD 2 (the frozen canonical record) and DoD 6 (the gate) belong here. DoD 1 and 3 are owned by slice 3; DoD 4 and the real-store half of DoD 5 are owned by slice 4. I am NOT silently narrowing a DoD — the rail forbids that and I am disclosing it instead: the DoD needs re-scoping to slice 1 by a governor or human, and this plan is written against the slice, not against the stale six-item list. Grading this plan against DoD 4's 'durably commit' clause would be grading it against work that now has an owner task id.

WHY SLICE 1 KEEPS THIS TASK ID rather than the normalizer, which matches the title better: slice 1 is the only slice with no unmet dependency, so it ships value now instead of parking this id behind three siblings. The title is consequently broader than the slice — a retitle to something like 'Provider-run telemetry record contract' would be accurate.

MIRROR THE LANDED TEMPLATE, DO NOT INVENT A SHAPE. apps/daemon/src/activation/activation-ledger-contracts.ts (244 lines) already solves this exact problem for the activation ledger and encodes two decisions worth borrowing whole: a NARROW store port that names only the commit surface it needs, and a derived aggregate id that makes conflict a store concern rather than a hand-rolled check.
